title: adaptive filtered vector search — the real axis is PROBES, not strategy (SIFT1M, real neighbors)
verdict: DESIGN-DRIVING MEASUREMENT — adaptive=selectivity-driven probes (INLINE⇄POST strategy switch FALSIFIED on real data)

dataset.name: SIFT1M
dataset.note: REAL neighbor structure — recall@10 is meaningful across the WHOLE selectivity range, unlike synthetic well-separated clusters which go tie-dense at loose selectivity

labels.assignment: bucket b assigned to floor(SEL[b]*N) rows, rest label 99, shuffled

ground_truth: exact seqscan-filtered top-10 (WHERE lbl && '{L}' ORDER BY e <-> q LIMIT 10), same 100 SIFT queries

sweep_fixed_probes_64.note: INLINE (M90 v7) vs POST (M87 v5) at the default probes=64 across selectivity

finding_1_no_strategy_crossover: INLINE (v7) DOMINATES POST (v5) on recall at EVERY selectivity (0.74-0.95 vs 0.33-0.79). A 2-way INLINE⇄POST adaptive switch is FALSIFIED — POST never wins. The M91 premise 'different fixed strategies win in different regimes' does NOT hold on real data for this pair.
finding_2_synthetic_artifact: The pre-SIFT synthetic sweep (500k, 200 well-separated clusters, scale 20) showed a fake recall COLLAPSE at loose selectivity (INLINE 0.088 @ 30%). That was 100% a TIE-DENSITY artifact — with 2500 pts/cluster the true top-10 are hundreds of near-ties, so recall@10 is a coin-flip; probing all 200 lists did NOT help (base unfiltered recall stuck at 0.024 @ probes=200). On SIFT (real neighbors) the collapse VANISHES: INLINE holds 0.85-0.95 across 0.5%-30%. Measurement-first caught a phantom before any code was written.

probe_recovery_ultra_selective.note: at ultra-selective, does cranking probes recover INLINE recall? YES — decisively

finding_3_the_real_adaptive_axis: The adaptive axis is PROBES driven by the label selectivity, NOT a strategy switch. At 0.01% (100 matching rows), probes 64->500 lifts recall 0.741->1.000 (the true filtered NN hide in unprobed lists; more probes finds them). At 0.1%, probes 64->256 lifts 0.886->0.996. At 1%+ (already >=0.95), probes barely helps (flat). So the correct M91: the v7 INLINE scan should PROBE MORE LISTS when the filter is selective (few matching candidates per list), automatically — self-tuning on the measured matching-candidate count — so filtered recall stays high across the whole selectivity range without the user hand-tuning probes.
boundary: REAL data (SIFT1M) so recall is meaningful; the earlier synthetic collapse was a tie-density artifact (documented)

the M87 iterative re-search does NOT auto-recover this: it grows probes only when the heap UNDERFLOWS (< LIMIT candidates), but at ultra-selective the probed lists still yield >= LIMIT non-optimal matches, so LIMIT 10 is satisfied with a WRONG top-10 and growth never triggers — the M91 change fixes exactly this gap

at EXTREME selectivity (matches << rerank pool, e.g. <=0.001%) adaptive probing degenerates toward a near-full-list scan (O(lists) page reads) — bounded and correct (finding those few rows' NN has no cheaper path), but honest about the partial-read tension; a GUC ceiling is a follow-up only if measured needed
NOT a QPS-superiority claim vs ScaNN/AlloyDB (paradigm ceiling M73/M82 stands)

provenance.supersedes_synthetic: the 500k synthetic sweep is retained only as the tie-density counter-example
